title: Systematic staggered region evacuation chaos harness (tenant-aware shedding & rollback probes)
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Run controlled, staggered region-evacuation experiments that simulate partial network partitions, progressive GPU pool exhaustion, and synthetic dependency blackholes across a canary tenant set. The goal is to validate end-to-end failover behavior (traffic reroute, model variant fallback), verify circuit breaker and load-shedding thresholds, and measure SLO impact windows so we can tune automated rollback and tenant-priority policies.
acceptance_criteria: Create chaos harness that can: (a) isolate subset of control-plane signals in one region, (b) throttle and exhaust GPU allocators progressively, (c) inject dependency blackholes for datastore/cache layers.

For a 10-tenant canary cohort (mix of free/paid/enterprise), verify that high-priority tenants retain >= 99% of pre-failure throughput under graded degradation while P99 latency degradation remains within defined SLO windows for at most 5 minutes.
Circuit breakers trigger and open within configured thresholds (errors or tail latency) and downstream traffic is rerouted without client 5xx spikes > 2x baseline.
Automated rollback (control-plane switch to alternate-region routing) completes within target median 12s and documented playbook executes without manual intervention in 80% of runs.
Telemetry dashboards updated (per-tenant cost/latency breakdown) and a postmortem template populated after each run with metrics, decision points, and follow-ups.
steps: Design canary cohort and tenant weightings (balance enterprise, paid, free).
Instrument hybrid chaos controller with modes: partial-network-isolate, gpu-drain, dep-blackhole.
Add guardrails: runbook approval, kill-switch, quota limits (max 2 concurrent experiments), and strict maintenance window scheduling.
Implement telemetry queries and SLO gates (p99 latency, error rate, successful fallback percentage).
Execute dry-run in staging with synthetic traffic derived from replay traces. Log and iterate on failures.
Execute two controlled runs in us-west-1 during maintenance window; follow runbook and collect artifacts.
playbook: PRE-RUN: Notify oncall, ops, and SRE, open dedicated Slack channel #chaos-evac-eng-24680, ensure golden tracing enabled.
DURING-RUN: Start with partial-network-isolate for 60s, pause 5m, then escalate to gpu-drain at 25% allocation every 2 minutes up to 80%.
IF client error-rate > 3% AND fallback_success < 70%: abort and trigger immediate rollback to passive region.
POST-RUN: Run telemetry collectors, snapshot KV cache hit rates, container and GPU allocator logs, and capture model-variant latency profiles.
ROLLBACK: Use control-plane route override; validate egress paths, and confirm client-level request success by sampling 1000 requests across tenants.
risk_mitigation: Limit impact to explicitly-specified canary tenants and a synthetic traffic namespace.
Start in a staging region with a production-like config and only then repeat in a low-traffic production region during maintenance window.
Preflight checks to ensure cross-region capacity can absorb tenant reroutes (verify spare GPU headroom >= 30% before promoting run).
Two-person run approval from SRE lead and Product Ops required for production execution.
notes: Decision: use progressive GPU drain vs instant pool kill to observe graceful shedding behavior and KV cache priming effects.
Trade-off: progressive drains are slower to reveal some failure modes but better reflect realistic cloud contention patterns.
Design feedback from PM (Rohit Sinha): add per-tenant financial-impact metric to correlate shedding with unit cost increase.
Design feedback from Design (Lena O'Connor): dashboards need clearer colorblind-friendly palettes for per-tenant status pins.
